Sendust particles used were spherical with average diameters of approximately 5, 10, and 20 µm.
Composite samples contained 53 vol% sendust dispersed in polystyrene resin.
A metal-backed single-layer absorber with 20 µm sendust particles absorbed over 99% of electromagnetic waves above 20 GHz.
Composites with 5 µm particles showed return loss less than -20 dB below 10 GHz and above 30 GHz.
The real part of relative complex permeability µ’ for 5 µm particles approached about 0.9 at high frequencies.
µ’ for 10 µm and 20 µm particles approached approximately 0.81 and 0.7 respectively at high frequencies.
The imaginary part µ” decreased with frequency and was nearly zero for 5 µm particles at high frequencies.
The frequency dependence of µ* is influenced by natural magnetic resonance at low frequencies and eddy current effects at high frequencies.
Eddy currents flow on particle surfaces with skin depths smaller than particle size at high frequencies.
The nonreflective condition for absorption depends on µ* and ε* and sample thickness.
Polystyrene resin has a relative permittivity ε’ of about 19, assumed frequency independent.
Measurement of S-parameters was done using an Agilent 8722ES vector network analyzer.
The eddy current model predicts µ’ and µ” values that agree with measurements at high frequencies for large particles.
Ni-Zn ferrite and composites with aluminum or nickel particles were used to compare magnetic resonance and eddy current effects.
Sendust's magnetic properties allow flexible design of absorbers by tuning particle size and volume ratio.
The return loss of -20 dB corresponds to 99% absorption of electromagnetic wave power.
The composite thicknesses studied ranged from about 2.9 mm to 4 mm.
The absorption bandwidth normalized by center frequency varies with particle size.
The eddy current skin depths for aluminum and nickel particles at 1 GHz are approximately 2.6 µm and 1.3 µm respectively.
The study confirms that controlling particle size can tailor electromagnetic wave absorber performance across GHz frequency bands.
